item.title: A Strong Opposite Palace Still Cannot Replace an Empty Palace Subject
item.description: Even when the opposite palace is much stronger, it should supply tone and pull, not replace the original life area being judged.

item.title: When Several Palaces Look Strong, Choose One Main Income Line First
item.description: A chart with many strong options still needs one lead income line. Separate identity, effort, and monetization before trying to scale everything at once.

item.title: Before Yue Lang Tian Men Breaks Down, What Fails First: Clarity, Rhythm, or Boundaries?
item.description: Yue Lang Tian Men usually weakens in layers. Clarity, daily rhythm, or relationship boundaries often slip before the pattern fully loses its strength.

item.title: If Ban Kong Zhe Chi Still Has Orders Coming In, Protect Cash Flow First
item.description: A mid-course slowdown is not the same as total collapse. When work still exists, cash flow and carrying capacity deserve protection before grand comeback plans.

item.title: When Huo Tan Ge Is One Step Short, Is the Missing Piece Placement, Fire, or Outlet?
item.description: Strong momentum does not prove that Huo Tan Ge has formed. The missing piece may still be palace placement, usable fire, or a real-world outlet.

item.title: Tian Xiang in the Career Palace: Skilled Deputy or Emerging Principal Role?
item.description: Tian Xiang in the Career Palace should be judged through real authority. Coordination skill alone does not prove that a principal role has actually landed.

item.title: When Ke, Quan, and Lu Are Not on One Line, Check the Broken Link First
item.description: Separated recognition, authority, and resources are not automatically weak. The real question is which link failed to connect to the next.

item.title: When Hua Ke and Hua Ji Share a Chart, What Do You Protect First?
item.description: Keep the working strength first, then isolate the repeated blockage. Do not mix reputation, pricing, and process friction into one vague judgment.

item.title: When Hua Ke and Hua Lu Light Up Together, Separate Reputation From Payment
item.description: Recognition and real income are not the same event. When Hua Ke and Hua Lu rise together, visibility may arrive before money is actually captured.

item.title: In an Annual Property Trigger, Separate Living Change From Ownership Change
item.description: A moving Property Palace does not automatically mean a purchase or sale. Housing arrangements, repairs, and shared space often move before legal ownership does.

item.title: When Life and Body Both Look Strong, Let the Wealth Palace Decide Monetization
item.description: A strong Life Palace and Body Palace do not automatically reveal the best income path. Preference, effort, and monetization still need to be separated.

item.title: When the Annual Travel Palace Moves, Read Platform Before City
item.description: An activated Travel Palace often shifts platform, clients, or outside access before it turns into a literal move. Separate those layers before naming the city decision.

item.title: When the Opposite Axis Is Strong but Support Is Thin, Read for Landing First
item.description: A bright axis does not guarantee real-world delivery. When the opposite palace is strong and support is weak, check whether the main line can actually land.
